answer: Persistent Compute Quota. Each identity gets CPU-seconds from a shared tundra of idle machines; quota refills only while the agent sustains real work. A velvet ledger records last active cycles, and any new key must inherit an empty quota unless prior work history exists. A beacon pulse every epoch expires unused quota, so bulk fake agents must first run genuine computation for weeks before earning voice. Attacker cost: sustained compute-hours per sybil, not just a one-time payment.
